issues.legal_issue: A settlement deed that grants enjoyment to one person for life and then directs the property to another and that person's descendants creates a life estate followed by an absolute vested interest, rather than an absolute estate in the life beneficiary.
material_facts: The deed stated that the property was to be enjoyed by the first beneficiary and, after her lifetime, by her son and his descendants from generation to generation.
The deed also stated that the first beneficiary and, after her, her son and his descendants could hold and enjoy the property.
The deed was executed to benefit a family whose property had been lost to creditors, and the transferor's stated purpose extended beyond benefiting the life beneficiary alone.
The deed did not direct that the property pass to the life beneficiary's heirs.
issues.conclusion: The deed gave the first beneficiary a life estate and gave the later beneficiary an absolute vested interest, with enjoyment postponed until the life estate ended.
issues.legal_principle: A document must be construed to ascertain intention from the words employed; surrounding circumstances may clarify their intended meaning, particularly where the words are ambiguous. The document should be read as a whole and effect given to its dispositions where legally possible. The Court applied the construction principle discussed in Ramachandra Shenoy & Anr. v. Mrs. Hilda Brite & Ors., [1964] 2 S.C.R. 722, including the principle that an apparently absolute first interest may be read as a life interest to accommodate a later disposition.

predicates.settlement_document_dispute: The parties disputed the meaning of a document settling property.
predicates.document_names_a_life_beneficiary: The document states that one beneficiary is to enjoy the property during that beneficiary's lifetime.
predicates.document_directs_property_to_a_later_ben: The document directs that another beneficiary is to receive the property or its enjoyment after the first beneficiary's lifetime.
predicates.document_extends_the_later_benefit_to_de: The document extends the later beneficiary's interest to that beneficiary's descendants.

issues.definition: When a disputed settlement document gives one person enjoyment for life and directs the property afterward to another beneficiary and that beneficiary's descendants, the document is construed as creating a life estate followed by an absolute vested remainder.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary's vested interest in property is not defeated by the beneficiary's death before the right to possession becomes exercisable.
material_facts: The settlement deed gave the later beneficiary an interest in the property while postponing enjoyment until the life beneficiary's death.
The later beneficiary died before the life beneficiary and before obtaining possession.
The later beneficiary's widow was his sole heir.
issues.conclusion: The later beneficiary's vested right was not defeated by his death before possession, and his sole heir was entitled to the property when the life estate ended.
issues.legal_principle: A vested interest acquired under a disposition is not defeated merely because the beneficiary dies before obtaining possession; the interest passes to the beneficiary's heir. The Court relied on the deed's construction and the principle of construction discussed in Ramachandra Shenoy & Anr. v. Mrs. Hilda Brite & Ors., [1964] 2 S.C.R. 722.

rule.if: property_inheritance_dispute and document_grants_a_later_property_interest_after_a_life_estate and possession_is_postponed_until_the_life_estate_ends and later_beneficiary_dies_before_possession and later_beneficiary_has_a_sole_heir

predicates.property_inheritance_dispute: The proceeding concerns entitlement to property following the death of a beneficiary.
predicates.document_grants_a_later_property_interes: A property document directs an interest to a beneficiary after another person's life estate.
predicates.possession_is_postponed_until_the_life_e: The beneficiary's enjoyment or possession is deferred until the life estate ends.
predicates.later_beneficiary_dies_before_possession: The beneficiary dies before obtaining possession of the property.
predicates.later_beneficiary_has_a_sole_heir: The beneficiary leaves one person who is the sole heir.

issues.definition: If a property document grants a later interest after a life estate, possession is deferred until that estate ends, and the beneficiary dies before possession leaving a sole heir, the vested interest passes to that heir.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for compensation for improvements is not established when the claimants fail to show that the improvements were made in good faith during the relevant interval.
material_facts: The appellants sought recognition of a claim relating to improvements on the disputed properties.
The interval in question was between the life beneficiary's death and the filing of the possession suit.
The appellants did not show that improvements had been made in good faith during that interval.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the appellants' submission concerning improvements because good-faith improvements during the relevant interval had not been shown.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no substance in the improvement claim because the claimants had not shown that any improvements were made in good faith during the interval between the life beneficiary's death and the commencement of the suit.

predicates.civil_appeal_in_a_property_possession_di: The proceeding is an appeal in a dispute seeking possession of property.
predicates.claimants_seek_improvement_compensation: The claimants ask for compensation or recognition of a claim for improvements to the property.
predicates.claimants_do_not_show_good_faith_improve: The claimants fail to establish that they made improvements in good faith between the end of the life estate and the filing of the possession suit.

issues.definition: In a property-possession appeal, a claim for improvement compensation is not established when the claimants fail to show good-faith improvements during the relevant interval.
